claims.text: Equiatomic FeNiCrMn is an FCC high-entropy alloy under the stated conditions.
The initial material contains a baseline concentration of vacancy clusters.
Thermal vibrations influence the critical resolved shear stress without inducing a phase transformation in the stated temperature regime.
Shockley partial dislocations nucleate at vacancy clusters.
Shockley partial dislocation motion produces intrinsic stacking faults.
The deformation produces neither HCP phase nuclei nor twinning.
Dislocation nucleation at vacancy clusters is thermally activated.
Differences in Schmid factor between loading along <11-1> and <110> alter the resolved shear stress for partial-dislocation emission.
Differences in local atomic packing density along <11-1> and <110> alter the energy barrier for partial-dislocation emission.
The HCP-like regions are metastable stacking faults rather than products of a thermodynamic phase transformation.
The alloy's high stacking-fault energy stabilizes the HCP-like stacking-fault regions.
Yield strength decreases monotonically with increasing temperature.
Yield strength is relatively insensitive to strain rate from 10^8 to 10^10 s^-1.
Maximum yield stress differs significantly between loading along <11-1> and <110> because of orientation-dependent resolved shear stress.
The hypothesis does not specify which of the <11-1> and <110> orientations has the larger maximum yield stress.
The HCP-like regions have local atomic coordination corresponding to an ABAC stacking sequence.
The HCP-like regions lack the distinct lattice parameters and symmetry expected for a true HCP phase.
Local chemical short-range order can cause spatial variation in stacking-fault energy and hence in the magnitude of the orientation effect.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis and structural mediator state that vacancy clusters are the dislocation-nucleation sites, while the uncertainty field says the precise site cannot be confirmed and could instead be a grain boundary or surface defect.

The prediction says <11-1> will have significantly higher maximum yield stress than <110>, but immediately allows the reverse ordering; therefore it does not make a unique directional orientation prediction.
